title: Single-Instance Observables in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
abstract: We present a diagrammatic expansion for thermal expectation values of low-weight Majorana strings in a fixed realization of the $N$-fermion Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model. At each order in the expansion, the observable is expressed as a finite sum of polynomials in the couplings multiplied by temperature-dependent kernels built from the large-$N$ melonic propagator. At fixed $βJ$, the expansion is organized in powers of $N^{-1/2}$, and each order can be efficiently evaluated with classical resources polynomial in $N$. The expansion also extends to correlations at arbitrary imaginary times and sufficiently short real times. For the four-body SYK model, we show that the diagrammatic predictions give an excellent account of exact diagonalization results at sizes up to $N=24$. We also apply the method to the Maldacena--Qi (MQ) model formed from two identical copies of a fixed SYK realization. This enables the identification of a nearby SYK-like Hamiltonian whose thermofield double state has higher fidelity with the Maldacena--Qi ground state than the thermofield double of the original SYK Hamiltonian.
summary: This work presents a systematic diagrammatic expansion to calculate single-instance thermal observables in the SYK model, bypassing the need for disorder averaging. By organizing the calculation in powers of $N^{-1/2}$, the authors achieve results that match exact diagonalization for small systems and apply the technique to related models like MQ.
main_problem: The paper develops a method to compute single-instance thermal expectation values for low-weight Majorana strings in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model, moving beyond standard disorder averaging.
main_result: The diagrammatic expansion provides excellent quantitative agreement with exact diagonalization results for the four-body SYK model up to $N=24$, and it extends the analysis to the Maldacena–Qi (MQ) model.
method: The core method is a diagrammatic expansion organized in powers of $N^{-1/2}$, which expresses observables as finite sums of polynomials in couplings multiplied by temperature-dependent kernels derived from the large-$N$ melonic propagator.
model_or_system: The primary system is the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model, involving $N$ Majorana fermions with random $p$-body interactions (specifically $p=4$ is highlighted). The analysis is extended to the Maldacena–Qi (MQ) model.
key_observables: Single-instance thermal expectation values ($\xi_X$) of low-weight Majorana string operators, and time-ordered correlation functions.
important_parameters: The ratio $ eta J$ (inverse temperature times coupling strength) and the system size $N$. The expansion is organized in powers of $N^{-1/2}$.
main_assumptions: The method relies on a diagrammatic expansion which is treated as a dressed high-temperature expansion; convergence is noted to be non-uniform at low temperatures ($ eta J$ large).
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides an operator-by-operator preview comparing diagrammatic predictions to exact diagonalization results for $N=20,  eta J=2$, showing high fidelity ($R^2_{	ext{id}} = 0.9988$).
paper_structure: The paper details the diagrammatic expansion (Section 3), discusses corrections to leading diagrams (weight four study in Section 4), extends to time-dependent insertions (Section 5), and applies the method to the Maldacena–Qi (MQ) model (Section 6).
why_interesting: The ability to calculate single-instance, non-averaged thermal properties in highly entangled quantum systems like SYK is crucial for understanding quantum chaos and thermalization dynamics in strongly correlated regimes.

Figure 2: Melonic dressing for p = 4. (a) The self-energy insertion is a melon: two vertices (dots) joined by p −1 = 3 internal propagators, evaluating to Σ(τ) = J2G(τ)p−1 by the exact index count (27). (b) The Schwinger–Dyson equation (29) resumming the melon on every line: the dressed propagator G (thick) equals the bare propagator G0 (thin) plus one self-energy insertion followed by a dressed propagator.

Figure 3: ED weight-4 one-point values ξX versus the leading prediction −4I4(β)JX of (35), at βJ = 0.5, 1, 2 (left to right), for N = 10–20 (color). Each point is one weight-4 string of one disorder realization; both axes are normalized per N by the standard deviation of the predic- tion. Legends give the per-N through-origin slope; the diagonal is unit slope. The prediction is nearly exact at high temperature (slopes ≈1.01 at βJ = 0.5) and degrades smoothly as βJ grows, both the slope and the scatter increasing.

Figure 4: Through-origin slope of the ED weight-4 one-point values against the leading predic- tion −4I4(β)JX at βJ = 2, versus 1/N (N = 16–24; 160 disorder seeds, 48 operators per seed). The slope exceeds unity at finite N — about 1.11 at N = 16 — and falls almost linearly in 1/N toward the ideal value 1 (dashed); a fit s(N) = s∞+ a/N gives s∞≈1.00.
